source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Reproduction in Plants
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Eyes of potato that sprout into new plants are
questions.explanation: Each eye is a bud that vegetatively produces a new potato plant.

questions.stem: The innermost nutritive layer of the anther wall is the
questions.explanation: Tapetal cells nourish developing microspores and contribute to the pollen coat.

questions.stem: A typical shed pollen grain of angiosperms is
questions.explanation: In most flowering plants pollen is released at the 2-celled stage; the generative cell later forms two male gametes.

questions.stem: The mature Polygonum-type embryo sac is
questions.explanation: Seven cells (egg, two synergids, three antipodals, one central cell) hold eight nuclei.

questions.stem: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma of the same flower is
questions.explanation: Autogamy is self-pollination within one flower; xenogamy is pollen from another plant.

questions.stem: Self-incompatibility prevents
options: germination or growth of self pollen on the stigma
questions.explanation: A genetic recognition system blocks self pollen, promoting outbreeding.

questions.stem: Syngamy in flowering plants is the fusion of
options: a male gamete with the egg
questions.explanation: One sperm + egg = zygote (syngamy); the other sperm + polar nuclei = PEN (triple fusion).

questions.stem: The primary endosperm nucleus formed after triple fusion is
questions.explanation: Two polar nuclei (n + n) fuse with one male gamete (n) to give a 3n PEN.

questions.stem: A true fruit develops from the
questions.explanation: The ovary wall becomes pericarp; if the thalamus also ripens (apple), the fruit is false.

questions.stem: Apomixis is the formation of seeds
questions.explanation: An embryo arises without syngamy, so the seed is genetically maternal.

questions.stem: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically
questions.explanation: Pollen comes from another flower of the same plant, so the genomes are the same as in autogamy.

questions.stem: Triple fusion in the embryo sac involves a male gamete and
questions.explanation: The second sperm fuses with the two polar nuclei of the central cell.

questions.stem: In a typical anatropous ovule the micropyle lies
options: opposite the hilum and far from the funicle bend
close to the hilum because the body is inverted
questions.explanation: The ovule is inverted 180°, so micropyle and hilum come to lie near each other.

questions.stem: Water hyacinth spreads rapidly in water bodies by
questions.explanation: Offsets are short runners that clone new rosettes and make the weed invasive.

questions.stem: Microsporogenesis is the formation of
questions.explanation: Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to give a tetrad of haploid microspores.

questions.stem: The vegetative cell of a pollen grain
questions.explanation: The large vegetative cell grows the tube; the generative cell divides into two sperms.

questions.stem: The egg apparatus of the embryo sac consists of
questions.explanation: At the micropylar end, two synergids flank the egg and help the pollen tube discharge.

questions.stem: Xenogamy is pollination between
options: two flowers of the same plant
anther and ovule of one unopened bud
questions.explanation: Only xenogamy brings genetically different pollen; geitonogamy uses another flower of the same plant.

questions.stem: Cleistogamous flowers (as in Viola) ensure
questions.explanation: Closed flowers never open, so pollen lands on the stigma of the same flower.

questions.stem: Double fertilisation produces a zygote and
questions.explanation: Syngamy makes the zygote; triple fusion makes the 3n PEN that becomes endosperm.

questions.stem: The dicot embryo typically shows two
questions.explanation: Two cotyledons, a radicle and a plumule make the typical dicot embryo.

questions.stem: Albuminous seeds retain
options: only a perisperm and no embryo
questions.explanation: Castor and maize keep endosperm; pea and groundnut are exalbuminous because cotyledons store food.

questions.stem: Polyembryony (as in Citrus) means
options: one ovule never forms a seed
more than one embryo in a seed
questions.explanation: Several embryos, often from nucellar cells, occur in one Citrus seed.

questions.stem: Which statement about pollen is incorrect?
options: The generative cell always forms the pollen tube
questions.explanation: The vegetative cell grows the tube; the generative cell produces the two male gametes.

questions.stem: Dichogamy promotes outbreeding because
options: anther and stigma mature at different times
questions.explanation: Protandry or protogyny separates male and female phases so self-pollen is less likely to succeed.

questions.stem: Which pairing of seed or fruit type is incorrect?
options: Maize — no endosperm in the grain
questions.explanation: Maize grain is albuminous; a large endosperm remains as the food store.
